extraction.name: VOICEASSISTANT-EVAL
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.citeAs: VOICEASSISTANT-EVAL: BENCHMARKING AI ASSISTANTS ACROSS LISTENING, SPEAKING, AND VIEWING
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involved extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The data curation process involved deduplication, validation, categorization, and sampling to ensure data quality and reliability.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data collection involved source data from 23 audio understanding datasets and 22 text datasets for the Listening and Speaking subsets, and MMMU for the Viewing subset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The collected text instructions were converted into audio using three advanced text-to-speech (TTS) models: F5TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The data annotation process involved a triadic evaluation system, evaluating model responses across three key dimensions: content quality, speech quality, and consistency between them.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The evaluation metrics included gpt-oss-20b to assess response texts with thirteen evaluator prompts, UTMOS to measure speech quality, and a modified Word Error Rate (WER) to evaluate consistency between text and speech modalities.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The VoiceAssistant-Eval dataset and code for result reproduction will be publicly available under an MIT license.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, with strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to push the boundaries of what AI assistants can achieve and will be instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal models and in tracking progress toward truly expert AI assistants.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may still be limited in diversity, with a monolingual focus on English and a fixed set of 100 roles in the role-play subset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current benchmark has limitations, including a potential lack of diversity in the dataset, limited model evaluation, and reliance on automated measures and GPT-based scoring.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluating AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing tasks, with a focus on hands-free interaction, diverse audio contexts, and multimodal integration.
